subdivision_of_building: n/a. No work relating to buildings proposed.
description: Construction of a Artificial Grass Pitch (AGP) with perimeter fencing, hardstanding areas, storage container, floodlights and an access footpath
decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.
REASON
To comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.
The development hereby permitted shall not be carried out except in complete accordance with the details shown on the submitted plans, numbers:
02 Rev. 02 (Site Location Plan)
03 (Proposed Site Plan)
04 (Proposed AGP Plan)
05 (Proposed Elevation)
06 (Floodlighting Scheme)
07 (Proposed AGP Drainage Layout)

09 (Playing Field Layout)
10 (Infill Containment Measures)
11 Rev 01 (Site Sections)
12 (Pitch Sections)
13 (Pitch Levels)
14 (Indicative Groundworks Plan)
REASON
To ensure the development complies with the provisions of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012), Part 2 (2020) and the London Plan (2021).
The development hereby permitted shall be carried out and thereafter operated in accordance with the following approved supporting documents:
Sports Lighting Statement by Surfacing Standards Limited dated 3 December 2025
Floodlighting Performance Report by Surfacing Standards Limited dated 2 December 2025
Appendix D - Proposed Materials and Appearance by Surfacing Standards Limited
Drainage Strategy by Surfacing Standards Limited dated 3 December 2025
Noise Impact Assessment by Acoustic Consultants Ltd dated 23 December 2025
Transport Assessment by TPS Transport Consultants Ltd dated December 2025

The Statutory Biodiversity Metric dated 16 December 2025 completed by Patrick Collins
BNG Baseline V1
BNG Proposed V1
Phase II Bat Surveys by BJ Collins dated December 2025
Preliminary Ecological Appraisal (Extended) Report by BJ Collins dated December 2025
Design and Access with Planning Statement by Surfacing Standards Limited

The fencing, floodlighting columns, maintenance/storage container and associated structures hereby approved shall be finished and thereafter retained in the colours and materials specified within the approved plans and supporting documents unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The finishes shall thereafter be maintained as such for the lifetime of the development.
REASON

To ensure a satisfactory appearance and to safeguard the character and visual amenities of the area in accordance with Policy D4 of the London Plan (2021), Policy BE1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Policy DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020).
No development shall commence until a Construction Management Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Plan shall detail:
(i) The phasing of development works;
(ii) The hours during which development works will occur (please refer to informative I15 for maximum permitted working hours);
(iii) Measures to prevent mud and dirt tracking onto footways and adjoining roads (including wheel washing facilities);

(iv) Traffic management and access arrangements (vehicular and pedestrian) and parking provisions for contractors during the development process, including measures to reduce the number of construction vehicles accessing the site during peak hours;
(v) Measures to reduce the impact of the development on local air quality and dust through minimising emissions throughout the construction process;
(vi) The storage of construction materials on site;
(vii) Details of the anticipated volume, source and type of imported fill material associated

The development hereby approved shall be carried out in accordance with the submitted Arboricultural Impact Assessment by RPS dated 8th December 2025 and Tree Protection Plan contained therein (drawing no. 5477-RPS-XX-XX-DR-AR-91003). The approved tree protection measures shall be installed prior to commencement of development and retained for the duration of construction works.
REASON

To ensure that the proposed development will preserve and enhance the visual amenities of the locality and provide adequate facilities in compliance with policies DMHB 11 and DMHB 14 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020) and Policies G5, G6 and G7 of the London Plan (2021).

The development hereby approved shall be carried out in full accordance with the recommendations and mitigation measures contained within Section 5 of the Preliminary Ecological Appraisal (Extended) Report by BJ Collins dated December 2025. In addition, the following precautionary measures shall be implemented throughout construction works:
- A pre-commencement inspection for badger activity by a suitably qualified ecologist
- No open excavations left overnight
- Covering trenches or providing escape ramps
- Sensitive vegetation clearance
- No storage of chemicals/food waste accessible to badgers
- Toolbox talk for contractors.
REASON
In order to safeguard biodiversity and protected species, in accordance with policy DMEI 7 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020) and London Plan (2021) Policies G5 and G6.

No removal of trees, shrubs or other vegetation shall take place during the bird nesting season (1st March to 31st August inclusive) unless a survey for active nesting birds has first been undertaken by a suitably qualified ecologist and submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Where active nests are identified, an appropriate buffer zone shall be established and retained until the young have fledged and the nest is no longer in use.
REASON
To safeguard nesting birds and protected species in accordance with Policy DMEI 7 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020) and Policy G6 of the London Plan (2021).

No development shall commence until a Biodiversity Gain Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority demonstrating how a minimum 10% Biodiversity Net Gain will be achieved in accordance with Schedule 7A of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.
The approved Biodiversity Gain Plan shall thereafter be implemented and maintained in accordance with the approved details.
REASON

To ensure the development delivers a Biodiversity Net Gain and secures the protection and effective management of the remaining habitat on site in accordance with Section 15 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policy G6 of The London Plan (2021), and Policy DMEI 7 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020)

The development hereby approved shall be carried out in accordance with the Drainage Strategy by Surfacing Standards Limited dated 3rd December 2025 in addition to drawing nos. 08 (Proposed AGP Drainage Strategy) and 07 (Proposed AGP Drainage Layout). The approved drainage infrastructure shall be retained and maintained thereafter.
REASON

To ensure that surface water runoff is managed sustainably and to ensure that the development does not increase flood risk on site or elsewhere, in accordance with Policy SI13 of the London Plan (2021) and Policies DMEI 9 and DMEI 10 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020).

Prior to the removal of trees T15 and T16 identified within the approved Arboricultural Impact Assessment by RPS dated 8th December 2025, details of replacement tree planting and associated landscaping mitigation shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall include:
- The number, species, size and location of replacement trees
- Details of larger specimen tree planting where appropriate
- Planting specifications
- An implementation timetable
- Details of long-term maintenance and management.

The replacement planting strategy shall provide appropriate mitigation for the loss of trees T15 and T16 and shall have regard to the existing arboricultural and environmental value of the removed trees, informed by CAVAT or an alternative appropriate tree valuation methodology.
The approved replacement tree planting shall be carried out in the first planting season following completion of the development. Any replacement tree which, within a p

Prior to first use of the development hereby approved, a detailed hard and soft landscaping scheme, including landscaping of the engineered bund areas and all hard landscaped areas associated with the Artificial Grass Pitch (AGP), shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall include:
- Planting specifications
- Details of all hard surfacing materials
- Landscaping treatment to the bunded areas
- Implementation timetable
- Long-term maintenance and management arrangements.
The approved landscaping scheme shall be implemented in the first planting season following first use of the development and thereafter retained and maintained.
REASON

To ensure that the proposed development preserves and enhances the visual amenities of the locality and provides appropriate landscape mitigation in compliance with Policies DMHB 11 and DMHB 14 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020) and Policies G1, G5 and G7 of the London Plan (2021).

Any tree, shrub or area of planting forming part of the approved landscaping scheme which, within a period of five years from the completion of the landscaping scheme, dies, is removed, becomes seriously damaged or diseased shall be replaced in the next planting season with another of similar size and species, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
REASON

To ensure that the proposed development preserves and enhances the visual amenities of the locality in compliance with Policies DMHB 11 and DMHB 14 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020) and Policies G1, G5 and G7 of the London Plan (2021).

The floodlighting hereby approved shall be installed, operated and maintained in accordance with the approved Sports Lighting Statement by Surfacing Standards Limited dated 3rd December 2025, the Floodlighting Performance Report and drawing no. 06 (Floodlighting Scheme). The lighting system shall thereafter be retained and operated only in accordance with the approved details.
REASON
To safeguard residential amenity and ecological interests in accordance with Policies DMHB 11 and DMEI 7 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020) and Policies D14 and G6 of the London Plan (2021).

Prior to the first use of the floodlighting hereby approved, a post-installation lighting verification report shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority demonstrating that the installed lighting complies with the approved lighting scheme and illumination levels. The lighting shall thereafter be retained in accordance with the approved details.
REASON
To safeguard residential amenity and ecological interests in accordance with Policies DMHB 11 and DMEI 7 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020) and Policies D14 and G6 of the London Plan (2021).
The Artificial Grass Pitch (AGP) hereby approved, including all floodlighting, shall only operate between the following hours:
Monday to Friday: 08:00 - 21:00 (final curfew at 21:15)
Saturday: 08:00 - 20:00 (final curfew at 20:15)
Sundays and Bank Holidays: 09:00 - 18:00 (final curfew at 18:15)
Outside of these hours the AGP and floodlighting shall not be used.
REASON
To safeguard the residential amenity of neighbouring occupiers in accordance with Policy DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020) and Policy D14 of the London Plan (2021).

Prior to first use of the development hereby approved, and notwithstanding the details already submitted, an updated Noise Management Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Noise Management Plan shall include details of:
- Management responsibilities
- Measures to minimise noise and anti-social behaviour
- Complaints procedures and contact arrangements
- Monitoring and review procedures
- Maintenance arrangements for the AGP and perimeter fencing.
The Noise Management Plan shall reflect the approved hours of use of the development and shall thereafter be implemented and maintained for the lifetime of the development.
REASON

To safeguard the residential amenity of surrounding occupiers, in accordance with Paragraph 135(f) of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policy D3 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020).

Prior to the first use of the Artificial Grass Pitch (AGP) hereby approved, a Community Use Agreement prepared in consultation with Sport England shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The agreement shall apply to the Artificial Grass Pitch, Cricket Wickets and associated facilities and include details of pricing policy, hours of use, access by non-educational establishment users, management responsibilities and a mechanism for review. The development shall not be used otherwise than in strict compliance with the approved agreement.
REASON

To secure well-managed, safe community access to the sports facility/facilities, to ensure sufficient benefit to the development of sport, in accordance with Policies S5 of the London Plan (2021), CI1 and EM5 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012), DMCI 2 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020) and paragraph 93 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024).

Prior to the commencement of development of the Artificial Grass Pitch (AGP) hereby permitted, the Artificial Cricket Wickets hereby approved shall be installed and ready for use and the Artificial Cricket Wickets shown for removal on drawing no. 03 (Proposed Site Plan), shall be removed.
REASON

To ensure that playing cricket at the site is not adversely affected during and after the development of the Artificial Grass Pitch (AGP), thereby not detrimentally affecting sport, in accordance with Policies S5 of the London Plan (2021) and EM5 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012).

The Artificial Grass Pitch (AGP) hereby permitted shall be designed, constructed and maintained in accordance with World Rugby Regulation 22 Specification and shall thereafter be retained in accordance with World Rugby Regulation 22 Specification for as long as the AGP hereby permitted remains in existence.
REASON

To ensure that the facility is designed to be fit for rugby play and to meet wider community needs, in accordance with Policies S5 of the London Plan (2021) and EM5 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012).

Prior to first use of the development hereby approved, a minimum of 1 staff cycle parking space and 1 cycle parking space per 20 patrons shall be made available within the existing cycle parking provision on the wider school site and thereafter retained for such purposes.
REASON
To ensure adequate provision for cyclists in accordance with Policies T4 and T5 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy DMT 5 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020).

The decision to GRANT planning permission has been taken having regard to all relevant planning legislation, regulations, guidance, circulars and Council policies, including The Human Rights Act (1998) (HRA 1998) which makes it unlawful for the Council to act incompatibly with Convention rights, specifically Article 6 (right to a fair hearing); Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life); Article 1 of the First Protocol (protection of property) and Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination).

The decision to GRANT planning permission has been taken having regard to the policies and proposals in the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Part 2 (2020) set out below, including Supplementary Planning Guidance, and to all relevant material considerations, including The London Plan (2021) and national guidance.

Nuisance from demolition and construction works is subject to control under The Control of Pollution Act 1974, the Clean Air Acts and other related legislation. In particular, you should ensure that the following are complied with:-

A. Demolition and construction works which are audible at the site boundary shall only be carried out between the hours of 08.00 and 18.00 hours Monday to Friday and between the hours of 08.00 hours and 13.00 hours on Saturday. No works shall be carried out on Sundays, Bank or Public Holidays.
B. All noise generated during such works shall be controlled in compliance with British Standard Code of Practice BS 5228:2009.
C. Dust emissions shall be controlled in compliance with the Mayor of London's Best Practice Guidance' The Control of dust and emissions from construction and demolition.
D. No bonfires that create dark smoke or nuisance to local residents.
You are advised to consult the Council's Environmental Protection Unit (www.hillingdon.gov.uk/nois

In dealing with the application the Council has implemented the requirement in the National Planning Policy Framework to work with the applicant in a positive and proactive way. We have made available detailed advice in the form of our statutory policies from Local Plan Part 1, Local Plan Part 2, Supplementary Planning Documents, Planning Briefs and other informal written guidance, in order to ensure that the applicant has been given every opportunity to submit an application which is likely to be considered favourably.
